entries.title: Clashes erupt in Barcelona after thousands join Spain general strike
entries.snippet: Tens of thousands of people have been taking part in the strike, called by the country's main unions over housing and the high cost of living.

entries.title: Kidnapper, 74, escapes from house arrest in Argentina by abseiling from balcony
entries.snippet: Leonardo Bertulazzi, a former member of the Marxist guerrilla group the Red Brigades, was about to be extradited to his home country of Italy.

entries.title: Schools in Italy, Scotland and Northern Ireland hit by threats in suspected bomb hoax
entries.snippet: More than 6,000 Italian schools received a threat. Authorities in all three countries say there appears to be no risk to the public.

entries.title: Kenya discharges last Ebola patient in major milestone towards virus-free status
entries.snippet: The country begins a 42-day countdown to being declared Ebola-free, provided no new cases are recorded.

entries.title: Egyptian journalist's retrial adjourned as UN warns of 'assaults on press freedom'
entries.snippet: Mada Masr editor-in-chief Lina Attalah is being tried on the charge of "publishing false news" and potentially faces imprisonment.

entries.title: Vinícius Jr sends message to Sudan boy who received prosthetic legs after BBC report sparks appeal

entries.snippet: Trump welcomes the outcome, praising Hegseth as a "Great American Patriot", but Democrats can try again next year.

entries.title: Haitian PM praises El Salvador after joint strike on alleged home of gang leader
entries.snippet: The 400 Mawozo gang was targeted by El Salvador's military, which has deployed thousands of troops to combat Haiti's gang violence crisis.

entries.title: Watch: Vinícius Jr's surprise message to boy who received prosthetic legs after Sudan drone strike
entries.snippet: Real Madrid player Vinícius Jr sent a surprise message to 13-year-old fan Zaher who lost both his legs after being hit by a drone in Khartoum, in 2024.

entries.title: Watch: E-bike battery explodes into massive fireball inside Oregon home
entries.snippet: Surveillance footage from inside the home shows a mother and son noticing smoke coming from the battery before it suddenly bursts into flames.

entries.snippet: Democrat Scott Colom has won election to the U.S. Senate in Mississippi, according to a race call by the Associated Press, defeating Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith.

entries.title: Why is gasoline suddenly under $4 a gallon?
entries.snippet: The average price of a gallon of gasoline dipped below $4 this week for the first time in months. Does that mean more relief is coming for drivers?

entries.title: Greetings from Senegal, where breakdancers are competing in the Youth Olympics
entries.snippet: Senegal's breakdancers have been practicing for their country's historic hosting of the Youth Olympic Games this month. It's the first time Africa is hosting an Olympic event.

entries.title: Kennedy relatives join the fight against Trump's arch, alleging harm to JFK's grave
entries.snippet: Nine members of the Kennedy family have joined the legal fight against Trump's D.C. arch, arguing it would disrupt views and cast shadows over their ancestors' graves at Arlington National Cemetery.

entries.title: What's behind democratic socialists' historic victories in the midterms?
entries.snippet: Historian and The New Yorker writer Jill Lepore says the DSA, once maligned, is no longer "beyond the political pale." She discusses the history of socialism in America, and its current resurgence.

entries.title: Following big Democratic wins, these swing voters are looking for results
entries.snippet: For the swing voters NPR is regularly checking in with as part of its Swing Shift series, the election results brought mixed emotions, as does the pending Democratic control of Congress.

entries.title: Russia and Ukraine agree to a prisoner exchange as talks end with no big breakthrough
entries.snippet: Russia and Ukraine have agreed to a large exchange of prisoners of war. U.S.-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi led to this decision, marking the biggest humanitarian release since the war began in 2022.

entries.title: House effectively ends Hegseth impeachment. And, 3 men accused of plotting U.K. attacks
entries.snippet: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has been spared from the House's impeachment effort, at least for now. And, federal prosecutors arrested three men accused of being Iran-backed operatives.

entries.title: An Iran-backed trio is accused of plotting attacks on a U.K. base hosting U.S. jets
entries.snippet: Iran-backed operatives have been charged over nearly 20 attacks, including a plot on a U.K. base housing U.S. troops. Separately, a U.S. soldier is held in the U.K. on Russia spying claims.

entries.title: Indictment sheds light on alleged Iran-backed plots across U.S. and Europe

entries.snippet: The themes of service to country and reflection on humanity are at the center of the new film "The Mosquito Bowl." Special correspondent Mike Cerre caught up with some of the forces behind the film and the real historical event. It's part of our arts and culture series, CANVAS.

entries.title: Scott Colom wins Senate election in Mississippi
entries.snippet: Democratic nominee Scott Colom has defeated Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith in Mississippi's closely contested U.S. Senate race after a prolonged ballot counting process, giving the state its first Black U.S. senator since post-Civil War Reconstruction.

entries.title: Russia and Ukraine agree to a large prisoner exchange as talks end with no major breakthrough
entries.snippet: Russia and Ukraine agreed to a large exchange of prisoners of war, both sides said Wednesday as two days of U.S.-mediated talks concluded with no major breakthrough on ending Moscow's nearly 5-year-old full-scale invasion.

entries.title: Biden says he wouldn't have run for a second term in 2024 if he knew he had cancer
entries.snippet: Joe Biden says he did not know he had cancer while he was president and would not have sought a second term if he already had been diagnosed.

entries.title: Judge allows Trump defamation case against BBC to proceed but tosses 1 claim
entries.snippet: President Donald Trump's $10 billion defamation case against the BBC remains on track, for the moment.

entries.title: Trump says the towering arch he wants to be build might be dedicated to military veterans
entries.snippet: President Donald Trump observed Veterans Day by suggesting that the towering arch he wants to build in his own honor would also be dedicated to the U.S. military and those who served in its ranks.

entries.title: Missing South Carolina infant rescued after being buried alive in a dog crate for 24 hours
entries.snippet: When an 11-month-old infant was reported missing in South Carolina, dozens of first responders combed the countryside for the "bright boy with reddish blond hair" who, the sheriff's office said, had disappeared while his grandmother ran errands.

entries.title: More than a dozen key races remain too early to call one week after Election Day
entries.snippet: The size of Democrats' majorities in the House and Senate remained undetermined one week after Election Day as more than a dozen races were still too early to call Tuesday.

entries.snippet: Extramarital affairs are usually private matters. Jensen Huang's has global implications.

entries.title: Read the letter the White House's top lawyer sent Rep. Garcia over threats to investigate Trump
entries.snippet: The White House's top lawyer sent a letter of warning to incoming House Oversight Committee chair Rep. Robert Garcia, D-Calif., on Wednesday, claiming that the Democrats' promise to investigate the Trump administration "may cross the line into blatant criminality."

entries.title: WATCH LIVE: SS United States, once world's fastest ocean liner, sinks to become reef off Florida
entries.snippet: The historic ocean liner SS United States will be intentionally sunk Wednesday off the coast of the Florida panhandle.

entries.title: White House sends warning to Democrats about investigating the Trump administration
entries.snippet: The White House has issued a warning to Democrats over their planned probes into the Trump administration, going as far as claiming that such investigations — a standard oversight function of Congress -- may amount to "blatant criminality."

entries.title: DW
entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: Democrat Colom wins Mississippi Senate seat
entries.snippet: The southern US state of Mississippi has elected its first Black senator in more than 140 years. Democrat Scott Colom has won the seat in a historic upset, according to projections.

entries.title: Russian Foreign Ministry says its ambassador to US has died
entries.snippet: Russia's Foreign Ministry has said that Alexander Darchiev died from a chronic illness at the age of 66. The long-time diplomat had been in the Washington post since early 2025.

entries.title: Spain: Housing crisis prompts general strike, mass nighttime protests
entries.snippet: Hundreds of thousands of citizens have hit the streets to protest Spain's housing crisis after millions of union workers staged a general strike. The crisis has triggered snap elections to take place on November 29.

entries.title: Fears of rising antisemitism in Europe
entries.snippet: Holocaust survivor Regina Sluszny commemorates the victims of Auschwitz as Jewish communities across Europe face growing hostility. What does the promise of "Never Again" mean for Jewish life in Europe today?

entries.title: VW scraps production modernization plan citing tough financial straits
entries.snippet: VW has announced that it will scrap large-scale modernization in light of its current economic situation. Employee representatives accuse leadership of putting short-term profits before long-term company viability.

entries.title: Integration of immigrants in Germany: Much has been accomplished but problems remain
entries.snippet: The Federal office for Migration and Refugees has released a new Integration Report. It found that while the integration of people with a migrant history is improving, violent youth remain a problem.

entries.title: Democracy study: One-quarter of Germans want a right-wing authoritarian dictatorship
entries.snippet: The far-right AfD's electoral successes point to a new trend in Germany: Prejudice, resentment, and extremism are on the rise. A new study suggests satisfaction with democracy is at a low ebb.

entries.title: Kenya's last Ebola patient leaves hospital
entries.snippet: Kenya had nine confirmed cases, while DR Congo continues to battle its deadliest outbreak of the disease.

entries.title: Brazil electoral court fines Meta, sees no deliberate election bias
entries.snippet: The fine came after President Lula's coalition filed a complaint. The court said there was no evidence of intent to influence the election. Meta said it will defend itself against "false allegations."

entries.title: Is AIIB's complaint mechanism failing affected communities?
entries.snippet: The AIIB has a grievance redress mechanism for people affected by projects it finances. But those seeking to file a complaint face significant hurdles. Critics say reforms and greater transparency are needed.

entries.title: Wael Mohya could make German football history at 17
entries.snippet: At just 17, Gladbach forward Wael Mohya has earned his first Germany call-up. The dual-national talent has chosen the DFB path for now — and could soon make modern national-team history.

entries.title: Italy: Hundreds of schools evacuated after bomb threats
entries.snippet: Although the government believes the threat to be a hoax, it has nevertheless prompted concerns about "hybrid warfare" in Europe. Similar messages were sent in Northern Ireland, Ireland, and Bulgaria.

entries.title: Tundu Lissu: After escaping the death penalty, what does his guilty verdict mean for Tanzania's democracy?
entries.snippet: A treason trial could have meant death by hanging for Tanzanian opposition leader Tundu Lissu. Instead, he now faces four years in prison for incitement to unrest. Can voices of dissident truly be heard in the country?

entries.title: Germany news: Only 1/3 of Germans satisfied with state of democracy
entries.snippet: A new authoritarianism study has revealed a new low in satisfaction levels with the functioning of German democracy. Meanwhile, the Bundeswehr has banned Chinese-made drones. DW has more.

entries.title: Iran classes Argentina navy, air force as 'terrorist organizations'
entries.snippet: In a tit-for-tat move, Iran has said it now considers Argentina's navy and air force as "terrorist organizations." Tehran claimed Buenos Aires is responsible for further consequences.

entries.title: DW Science explainer on the default mode network: what your brain does when you aren't focusing on anything, and why it's important.
entries.snippet: Doing nothing might be the ultimate brain hack. When you're bored, the brain goes into default mode network. It's not only healthy for you, but it may also shape the very essence of your identity.

entries.title: India: CPCB addresses stark Delhi pollution data gap on Diwali night
entries.snippet: India's main pollution monitor has issued a clarification on a wide air quality data gap between official and private reporting in New Delhi that saw the city choked amid Diwali fireworks. DW has the latest.

entries.title: Germany slips in climate protection rankings as other countries make gains
entries.snippet: Record renewable energy growth is driving climate progress in some countries, but Germany and many major emitters are falling behind.

entries.title: How AI worsens online violence against Middle East women
entries.snippet: Women in the Middle East already have to deal with an above-average share of online harassment and violence. The proliferation of AI-enabled tools is making it worse.
